dedupe_keys.name: stress adjusted water framework for data centres aware us county level monthly water stress with workload scheduling rainwater harvesting and dry cooling

description: This preprint introduces a stress-adjusted water framework that scores data centre water consumption by when and where it happens, not by volume alone. It uses the AWARE-US model to capture county-level monthly water availability in the United States and extends the accounting to the off-site water footprint of electricity generation. On that basis it studies workload scheduling policies that jointly optimise water and carbon efficiency, the potential of rainwater harvesting as a supplemental supply, and the feasibility of dry cooling as a water-free alternative to evaporative cooling. Producer: Talukder, Rahim, Sen Gupta, Ren and Islam; submitted to arXiv on 15 June 2026, accepted at ACM e-Energy 2026. Coverage: United States counties. Access: paper on arXiv; no code or data link was read on the abstract page. Licence and cost: free to read; licence CC-BY-4.0 (the paper, as linked on its arXiv abstract page). Caveats: only the abstract page was read, and the OSF dataset of data centre locations mentioned in the search result was not confirmed. Simulation uses: it supports siting, scheduling and cooling decisions of data centres under local water stress and drought adaptation scenarios. Related records: none linked.
